mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate indicates monetary easing, which may stimulate economic activity and lead to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS decreases by >0.25% in one month
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS decreases but SPX 20-day returns are negative more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment suggests economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE increases by >0.5pp in one month
failure_condition: If UNRATE rises but SPX 20-day returns are positive more than 60% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing housing starts indicate strong demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If HOUST grows but SPX 60-day returns are negative more than 50% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment rises and employment falls, it signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If both UNRATE rises and PAYEMS falls but SPX 20-day returns are positive more than 50% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production growth indicates a strong supply chain, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO grows but SPX 60-day returns are negative more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: Slowing GDP growth indicates economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If GDPC1 growth slows but SPX 60-day returns are positive more than 50% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: High CPI levels suggest inflationary pressures, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If CPI is high but SPX 20-day returns are positive more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: High federal funds rates in a late-cycle expansion may lead to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS is high but SPX 60-day returns are positive more than 50% of the time.
